code 1\n\"\"\"T03: Editors write and Submit Guides; Admins Publish them (Seam 1: the\nconsole over HTTP).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport html\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\nfrom conftest import add_user, csrf_token, login\nfrom test_t02_heroes_patches import submit as fill_in\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef admin(client_as) -> TestClient:\n    \"\"\"An Admin, with Heroes and Patches 6.4 to 6.7 (6.7 current) in place.\"\"\"\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    for name_zh, name_en in [(\"瓦妮莎\", \"Vanessa\"), (\"杜利\", \"Dooley\")]:\n        fill_in(admin, \"/admin/heroes\", \"/admin/heroes\",\n               name_zh=name_zh, name_en=name_en)\n    for name in [\"6.4\", \"6.5\", \"6.6\", \"6.7\"]:\n        fill_in(admin, \"/admin/patches\", \"/admin/patches\", name=name)\n    return admin\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef editor(admin, client_as) -> TestClient:\n    return client_as(\"editor\")\n\n\ndef option_value(page: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The value of the <option> showing `label` on a rendered form.\"\"\"\n    match = re.search(rf'<option value=\"(\\d+)\"[^>]*>{re.escape(label)}</option>', page)\n    assert match, f\"no option labelled {label}\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\ndef choice(c: TestClient, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The value of the Hero or Patch picker option showing `label`.\"\"\"\n    return option_value(c.get(\"/admin/guides/new\").text, label)\n\n\nhero_id = patch_id = choice\n\n\ndef guide_fields(c: TestClient, **fields) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"A complete Guide form: Chinese text, Vanessa, the Current Patch.\"\"\"\n    defaults = {\"title_zh\": \"瓦妮莎海盗流\", \"body_zh\": \"## 终局阵容\\n\\n先拿船。\",\n                \"title_en\": \"\", \"body_en\": \"\",\n                \"hero_id\": hero_id(c, \"瓦妮莎（Vanessa）\"),\n                \"patch_id\": patch_id(c, \"6.7（当前版本）\")}\n    return defaults | fields\n\n\ndef new_guide(c: TestClient, **fields) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save a new Guide as a Draft; returns its edit page.\"\"\"\n    response = fill_in(c, \"/admin/guides/new\", \"/admin/guides\",\n                      **guide_fields(c, **fields))\n    assert response.status_code == 303, response.text\n    edit_page = response.headers[\"location\"]\n    assert re.fullmatch(r\"/admin/guides/\\d+/edit\", edit_page)\n    return edit_page\n\n\ndef form_values(page: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"What the Guide form on `page` would send unchanged: its text inputs,\n    textareas and selected options.\"\"\"\n    values = dict(re.findall(r'<input type=\"text\" name=\"(\\w+)\" value=\"([^\"]*)\"', page))\n    values |= dict(re.findall(r'<textarea name=\"(\\w+)\"[^>]*>(.*?)</textarea>', page,\n                              re.DOTALL))\n    for name, options in re.findall(r'<select name=\"(\\w+)\"[^>]*>(.*?)</select>', page,\n                                    re.DOTALL):\n        selected = re.search(r'<option value=\"(\\d*)\" selected', options)\n        values[name] = selected.group(1) if selected else \"\"\n    return {name: html.unescape(value) for name, value in values.items()}\n\n\ndef save(c: TestClient, edit_page: str, **fields):\n    \"\"\"Change some fields of a saved Guide, keeping the rest as they are.\"\"\"\n    current = form_values(c.get(edit_page).text)\n    return fill_in(c, edit_page, edit_page.removesuffix(\"/edit\"),\n                  **(current | fields))\n\n\ndef test_editor_saves_a_draft_and_edits_it_later(editor):\n    edit_page = new_guide(editor, title_zh=\"瓦妮莎海盗流\",\n                          body_zh=\"先拿船，再拿炮。\")\n    page = editor.get(edit_page)\n safe }}\n  </article>\n  {% else %}\n  <p>这篇攻略没有英文版，不会出现在英文网站上。</p>\n  {% endif %}\n{% endblock %}\n# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\ndecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n.env\n*.db\nsite/\n__pycache__/\n.pytest_cache/\n.venv/\n.claude/state/\n.DS_Store\nhooks/\nskills/\nstate/\nsettings.json  638B\nsettings.local.json  124B\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nCreates one Admin and one Editor, a few Heroes, a few Patches (the last\none, 6.7, becomes the Current Patch), and demo Guides in Draft, Submitted and\nPublished, made through the Guide workflow just as the console makes them. The passwords come from\nCMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD; there are no default passwords, so\nthe script refuses to run without both. Running it again leaves existing\naccounts, Heroes and Patches alone, and adds no Guides once any exist.\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed. Later tickets add\nother Game Terms, a Page and Tournament items.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sqlite3\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import accounts, db, game, guides, settings\n\n# Matches DEMO_USERS in tests/conftest.py (which uses its own fixed passwords).\nDEMO_USERS = [\n    # role, email, Display name, environment variable holding the password\n    (\"admin\", \"admin@example.test\", \"演示管理员\", \"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\"),\n    (\"editor\", \"editor@example.test\", \"演示编辑\", \"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\"),\n]\n\n# Official Chinese name, official English name.\nDEMO_HEROES = [\n    (\"瓦妮莎\", \"Vanessa\"),\n    (\"皮格马利翁\", \"Pygmalien\"),\n    (\"杜利\", \"Dooley\"),\n    (\"马克\", \"Mak\"),\n]\n# Oldest first, so the last one added is the Current Patch.\nDEMO_PATCHES = [\"6.5\", \"6.6\", \"6.7\"]\n\n# Author's role, Hero (English name), Patch, status reached, Chinese title,\n# Chinese body, English title, English body.\nDEMO_GUIDES = [\n    (\"editor\", \"Vanessa\", \"6.7\", \"draft\", \"瓦妮莎海盗船流（写作中）\",\n     \"## 思路\\n\\n先拿船，再找炮。终局阵容还在测试。\", \"\", \"\"),\n    (\"editor\", \"Dooley\", \"6.7\", \"submitted\", \"杜利核心流入门\",\n     \"## 终局阵容\\n\\n围绕核心，前期拿**能量**物品。\\n\\n## 运营\\n\\n第 5 天前定型。\",\n     \"Dooley core build for beginners\",\n     \"## Final lineup\\n\\nBuild around the core and take **energy** items early.\"),\n    (\"editor\", \"Pygmalien\", \"6.6\", \"published\", \"皮格马利翁经济流\",\n     \"## 思路\\n\\n前期攒钱，中期一次性升级。\", \"\", \"\"),\n    (\"admin\", \"Mak\", \"6.7\", \"published\", \"马克药水流（6.7）\",\n     \"## 终局阵容\\n\\n药水叠毒，配合治疗。\\n\\n| 天数 | 目标 |\\n|---|---|\\n| 1–4 | 拿药水 |\\n| 5+ | 叠毒 |\",\n     \"Mak potion build (6.7)\",\n     \"## Final lineup\\n\\nStack poison with potions and heal through the midgame.\"),\n]\n\n\ndef seed_guides(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:\n    admin = _seed_user(conn, \"admin\")\n    if guides.guides(conn, admin):\n        print(\"guides: some already exist, none added.\")\n        return\n    heroes = {hero.name_en: hero.id for hero in game.heroes(conn)}\n    patches = {patch.name: patch.id for patch in game.patches(conn)}\n    for (role, hero, patch, status, title_zh, body_zh,\n         title_en, body_en) in DEMO_GUIDES:\n        author = _seed_user(conn, role)\n        guide = guides.create(conn, author, guides.GuideFields(\n            title_zh=title_zh, body_zh=body_zh, title_en=title_en,\n            body_en=body_en, hero_id=heroes[hero], patch_id=patches[patch]))\n        if status != \"draft\" and guides.can_submit(author, guide):\n            guides.submit(conn, author, guide.id)\n        if status == \"published\":\n            guides.publish(conn, admin, guide.id)\n        print(f\"guide: created {title_zh} ({guides.STATUS_LABELS[status]}).\")\n\n\ndef _seed_user(conn: sqlite3.Connection, role: str) -> accounts.User:\n    email = next(email for r, email, *_ in DEMO_USERS if r == role)\n    user = accounts.user_with_email(conn, email)\n    assert user is not None, f\"{email} should have been created above\"\n    return user\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    missing = [var for *_, var in DEMO_USERS if not os.environ.get(var)]\n    if missing:\n        print(f\"Set {' and '.join(missing)} in .env (copy .env.example), then run \"\n              \"`uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py`.\")\n        return 1\n\n    for *_, var in DEMO_USERS:\n        if os.environ[var].startswith(\"change-me\"):\n            print(f\"Warning: {var} is still the .env.example placeholder. \"\n                  \"Change it in .env before anyone else can reach this console.\")\n\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        for role, email, display_name, var in DEMO_USERS:\n            try:\n                accounts.create_user(conn, email=email, password=os.environ[var],\n                                     role=role, display_name=display_name)\n            except accounts.Refused:\n                print(f\"{role}: {email} already exists, left unchanged.\")\n                continue\n            print(f\"{role}: created {email} (password from {var}).\")\n        for name_zh, name_en in DEMO_HEROES:\n            try:\n                game.add_hero(conn, name_zh=name_zh, name_en=name_en)\n            except game.Refused as refused:\n                print(f\"hero: {name_en} left unchanged ({refused.message})\")\n                continue\n            print(f\"hero: created {name_zh} ({name_en}).\")\n        for name in DEMO_PATCHES:\n            try:\n                game.add_patch(conn, name)\n            except game.Refused as refused:\n                print(f\"patch: {name} left unchanged ({refused.message})\")\n                continue\n            print(f\"patch: created {name}.\")\n        seed_guides(conn)\n    print(f\"Database: {settings.database_path()}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())","is_error":false}]}}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","hash":"58a52a3a5b076f9c50110ecca3612247b4655ddd71d3d86b11951c7ee0da8886","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01DLQtDMGoCmXVVtDXjBB2pC","content":"Launching skill: mattpocock-skills:tdd"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]}}

{"parentUuid":"122b0e8c-7121-415a-8db3-2f3d315591ac","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"7493681f-3081-4ce7-b0af-962af4863fe1","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"6213ef0e-8a58-4e6f-99bf-364a2b2ee3c6","timestamp":"2026-10-17T17:51:50.791Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01DLQtDMGoCmXVVtDXjBB2pC","session_id":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

test_a_guide_must_have_a_hero(editor):\n    response = fill_in(editor, \"/admin/guides/new\", \"/admin/guides\",\n                      **guide_fields(editor, hero_id=\"\"))\n    assert response.status_code == 400\n    assert \"请选择英雄\" in response.text\n    assert \"没有攻略\" in editor.get(\"/admin/guides\").text\n\n\ndef slug_of(c: TestClient, edit_page: str) -> str:\n    match = re.search(r\"网址名：<code>([^<]+)</code>\", c.get(edit_page).text)\n    assert match, \"edit page shows no slug\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\ndef test_a_new_guide_gets_the_slug_hero_slug_dash_id(editor):\n    edit_page = new_guide(editor)\n    guide_number = edit_page.split(\"/\")[3]\n    assert slug_of(editor, edit_page) == f\"vanessa-{guide_number}\"\n\n    second = new_guide(editor, hero_id=hero_id(editor, \"杜利（Dooley）\"))\n    assert slug_of(editor, second) == f\"dooley-{second.split('/')[3]}\"\n\n\ndef test_editing_the_title_or_hero_never_changes_the_slug(editor):\n    edit_page = new_guide(editor)\n    slug = slug_of(editor, edit_page)\n    save(editor, edit_page, title_zh=\"全新的标题\",\n         hero_id=hero_id(editor, \"杜利（Dooley）\"))\n    assert slug_of(editor, edit_page) == slug\n\n\ndef test_admin_changes_a_guides_slug_and_a_duplicate_is_refused(editor, admin):\n    first = new_guide(editor)\n    second = new_guide(editor)\n    response = save(admin, first, slug=\"vanessa-pirates\")\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert slug_of(editor, first) == \"vanessa-pirates\"\n\n    clash = save(admin, second, slug=\"vanessa-pirates\")\n    assert clash.status_code == 400\n    assert \"网址名 vanessa-pirates 已被另一篇攻略使用\" in clash.text\n    assert the Site build puts Published Guides online in Chinese and English.\n\nContent is set up through the console (Seam 1); what Readers get is checked in\nthe files `render_site` writes (Seam 2).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.publish import render_site\nfrom test_t03_guides import act, admin, editor, new_guide, slug_of  # noqa: F401\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef site(tmp_path) -> Path:\n    return tmp_path / \"site\"\n\n\ndef build(site: Path) -> Path:\n    return render_site(site)\n\n\ndef published_guide(admin: TestClient, editor: TestClient | None = None,\n                    **fields) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A Guide written by `editor` (or the Admin), Submitted and Published.\n    Returns its slug.\"\"\"\n    author = editor or admin\n    edit_page = new_guide(author, **fields)\n    if editor:\n        assert act(editor, edit_page, \"submit\").status_code == test_a_published_guide_gets_its_own_page(admin, site):\n    slug = published_guide(admin, title_zh=\"瓦妮莎海盗流\",\n                           body_zh=\"## 终局阵容\\n\\n先拿船。\")\n    html = page(build(site), f\"zh/guides/{slug}/\")\n    assert \"瓦妮莎海盗流\" in html\n    assert \"<h2>终局阵容</h2>\" in {"parentUuid":"e638540c-358a-42b8-8bbe-f4b7634213c1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg8EkUPcVHzcxiz4xFPpB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HVYrG9nHRhGzP8gbnU9QxZ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/publish.py","content":"\"\"\"The Site build: render everything Published into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nThe site has a Chinese tree (zh/) and an English tree (en/), and every page is\nan index.html in its own folder, so its address is the folder (`zh/guides/\nvanessa-12/`). Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is read here. A Draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"../../style.css\"), never root-absolute\n     (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import db, guides, settings\nfrom app.rendering import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, \"PingFang SC\", \"Microsoft YaHei\", sans-serif;\n       margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .5rem 1rem; align-items: baseline; }\nheader .brand { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; margin-inline-end: auto; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\nLANGUAGES = (\"zh\", \"en\")\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    env = Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n    # `guide|localized(\"title\", lang)` is guide.title_zh or guide.title_en.\n It acts for no one, so it needs no user.\"\"\"\n    rows = conn.execute(f\"{_SELECT} WHERE guides.status = 'published'\"\n                        \" ORDER BY guides.updated_at DESC, guides.id DESC\").fetchall()\n    return [_guide_from_row(row) for row in rows]\n\n\ndef authors(conn: sqlite3.Connection, actor: User) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HVYrG9nHRhGzP8gbnU9QxZ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/publish.py","content":"\"\"\"The Site build: render everything Published into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nThe site has a Chinese tree (zh/) and an English tree (en/), and every page is\nan index.html in its own folder, so its address is the folder (`zh/guides/\nvanessa-12/`). Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is read here. A Draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"../../style.css\"), never root-absolute\n     (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import db, guides, settings\nfrom app.rendering import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, \"PingFang SC\", \"Microsoft YaHei\", sans-serif;\n       margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .5rem 1rem; align-items: baseline; }\nheader .brand { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; margin-inline-end: auto; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\nLANGUAGES = (\"zh\", \"en\")\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    env = Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n    # `guide|localized(\"title\", lang)` is guide.title_zh or guide.title_en.\n    env.filters[\"localized\"] = lambda item, field, lang: getattr(item, f\"{field}_{lang}\")\n    env.filters[\"markdown\"] = render_markdown\n    return env\n\n\nclass _Writer:\n    \"\"\"Writes pages into `out`, each given the relative way back to the root.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, out: Path) -> None:\n        self.out = out\n        self.env = environment()\n\n    def page(self, path: str, template: str, **context: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Write the page Readers get at `path`: \"\" for the root, or a folder\n        such as \"zh/guides/vanessa-12/\".\"\"\"\n        file = self.out / path / \"index.html\"\n        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        file.write_text(self.env.get_template(template).render(\n            root=\"../\" * path.count(\"/\"), **context))\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        published = guides.published(conn)\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    write = _Writer(out)\n    write.page(\"\", \"public/home.html\", title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[],\n               css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\")\n    for lang in LANGUAGES:\n        for guide in published:\n            write.page(f\"{lang}/guides/{guide.slug}/\", \"site/guide.html\",\n                       lang=lang, guide=guide)\n    return out\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","hash":"bb7222912856f22dfa787029ba953343360b3edfe3c3a491d9717f81acf81830","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01NHXqXkyHN4ZbWGUUJjZ5XV","content":"Launching skill: mattpocock-skills:code-review"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the uncommitted T04 changes (working tree vs HEAD), limited to these files: app/accounts.py app/cli.py app/db.py app/guides.py app/main.py app/publish.py app/rendering.py app/routes/dashboard.py app/routes/site.py templates/admin/dashboard.html templates/site/ tests/conftest.py tests/test_t04_site_build.py. Ignore scripts/usage_report.py, notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts (another session's work). Spec: GitHub issue #5 (T04), parent spec #1."}]}}

Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the uncommitted T04 changes (working tree vs HEAD), limited to these files: app/accounts.py app/cli.py app/db.py app/guides.py app/main.py app/publish.py app/rendering.py app/routes/dashboard.py app/routes/site.py templates/admin/dashboard.html templates/site/ tests/conftest.py tests/test_t04_site_build.py. Ignore scripts/usage_report.py, notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts (another session's work). Spec: GitHub issue #5 (T04), parent spec #1."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"72e8529e-3ed2-48fc-8c14-5393884cec8e","timestamp":"2026-10-17T18:01:47.309Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01NHXqXkyHN4ZbWGUUJjZ5XV","session_id":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","hash":"736e25f52f71b91fc07894ae94ff1d0d7f172cef2790a38eb77194514aa6f895","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015Gj6D79eYRKf3jW3Sb8shd","type":"tool_result","content":"ls: CODING_STANDARDS.md: No such file or directory\nls: CONTRIBUTING.md: No such file or directory\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.\nefb239d2d3c8a99550d1f95970ae97f5282cd1a8\napp/accounts.py                |   1 +\n app/cli.py                     |  23 +++---\n app/db.py                      |  16 +++-\n app/guides.py                  |  23 ++++--\n app/main.py                    |   3 +-\n app/publish.py                 | 170 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-----\n app/rendering.py               |  13 +++-\n app/routes/dashboard.py        |   6 +-\n templates/admin/dashboard.html |   9 +++\n tests/conftest.py              |  17 ++++-\n 10 files changed, 237 insertions(+), 44 deletions(-)","is_error":false}]}}

Skip anything tooling enforces.\n- Mysterious Name: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it.\n- Duplicated Code: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file. → extract the shared shape.\n- Feature Envy: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move it onto that data.\n- Data Clumps: the same few fields or params keep travelling together. → bundle into one type.\n- Primitive Obsession: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept. → give it its own small type.\n- Repeated Switches: the same switch/if-cascade on the same type recurs. → polymorphism or one shared map.\n- Shotgun Surgery: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files. → gather into one module.\n- Divergent Change: one file edited for several unrelated reasons. → split.\n- Speculative Generality: abstraction, params or hooks for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it.\n- Message Chains: long a.b().c().d() navigation. → hide behind one method.\n- Middle Man: a class/function that mostly delegates. → cut it.\n- Refused Bequest: a subclass that ignores most of what it inherits. → composition.\n\n**Brief:** Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Skip anything tooling enforces.\n- Mysterious Name: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it.\n- Duplicated Code: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file. → extract the shared shape.\n- Feature Envy: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move it onto that data.\n- Data Clumps: the same few fields or params keep travelling together. → bundle into one type.\n- Primitive Obsession: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept. → give it its own small type.\n- Repeated Switches: the same switch/if-cascade on the same type recurs. → polymorphism or one shared map.\n- Shotgun Surgery: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files. → gather into one module.\n- Divergent Change: one file edited for several unrelated reasons. → split.\n- Speculative Generality: abstraction, params or hooks for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it.\n- Message Chains: long a.b().c().d() navigation. → hide behind one method.\n- Middle Man: a class/function that mostly delegates. → cut it.\n- Refused Bequest: a subclass that ignores most of what it inherits. → composition.\n\n**Brief:** Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Everything else is a judgement call. The full suite passes (138 tests), but only because `templates/site/` exists on this disk.\n\n**Hard violations**\n\n- **`templates/site/*.html` (all seven files)**: `.gitignore` line 3 is `site/`. That pattern matches any folder named `site`, so `git check-ignore` confirms the T04 templates are ignored. They don't show in `git status` and would be left out of the commit. A clean clone would then fail the Site build, which breaks ADR-002's \"gradable from a clean clone\". Fix: change the pattern to `/site/`.\n\n**Judgement calls against documented standards**\n\n- **`cli.py` publish/deploy versus `publish.site_build()`**: `cms publish` plus `cms deploy` never inserts a `site_builds` row. After a Site build from the command line, the dashboard keeps saying \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\". CONTEXT.md treats the Site build as one step, but there are now two routes to it and only one is recorded.\n- **Vocabulary (CONTEXT.md)**: In `guide.html`, \"This guide has no English version\" uses \"version\", which is an _Avoid_ word (the glossary's own term is English text). The test name `test_admin_puts_the_site_online_with_the_update_site_button` avoids saying Site build. Calling the push sub-step `deploy` is fine, since spec #1 uses \"Deploy (the git push)\" the same way.\n- **Tests (spec #1, Testing Decisions)**: these comply. They go through HTTP and `render_site(out)`, never DB rows.\n\n**Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n\n- **Mysterious Name / inconsistent naming:** `publish.site_build()`, the route `build_site`, the dependency `site_builder` and the capability `\"build_site\"`. That's four spellings of one concept.\n- **Duplicated Code:**\n  - `site_builder` repeats `web.admin_user` (`if not user.can(...): raise AdminRequired`). A shared `requires(capability)` would remove the copy.\n  - The other-language rule is written twice: `other = \"en\" if lang == \"zh\" else \"zh\"` in `publish.py`, and `{{ \"en\" if lang == \"zh\" else \"zh\" }}` in `base.html`.\n  - `{% if guides %}{{ guide_list(guides) }}{% else %}&lt;p&gt;{{ t.no_guides }}&lt;/p&gt;{% endif %}` appears in both `home.html` and `author.html`, so it could live inside the macro.\n  - Suppressed: `DeployFailed` copies the `Refused(message)` shape, but that is the repo's convention.\n- **Feature Envy:** `changes_not_on_site` loads every Published Guide through `guides.published(conn)` just to compare `updated_at`. A count query in `guides.py` would keep it next to the data.\n- **Divergent Change:** `publish.py` now changes for four unrelated reasons: rendering, the git subprocess, recording builds in the DB, and dashboard counts.\n- **Speculative Generality:**\n  - `_Writer(out, **shared: Any)` only ever receives `current_patch`.\n  - The default `deploy(..., message=\"Publish site\")` is never needed, because both callers pass their own value.\n- **Primitive Obsession:**\n  - `lang` is a bare `\"zh\"`/`\"en\"` string throughout.\n  - Page paths are strings whose meaning depends on a trailing `/` (`relative()`'s `target.endswith(\"/\") or not target`).\n\n**No issues found** on CSRF (the form has its token and the app-wide `verify_csrf` covers it), relative paths in published HTML, Markdown sanitizing (`attribute_filter` now also drops `/` and `\\` URLs), Published-only reads (`guides.published`), dependencies (only stdlib and the existing `ghp_import`), or secrets.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>62379</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>7</tool_uses><duration_ms>85238</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

That pattern matches any folder named `site`, so `git check-ignore` confirms the T04 templates are ignored. They don't show in `git status` and would be left out of the commit. A clean clone would then fail the Site build, which breaks ADR-002's \"gradable from a clean clone\". Fix: change the pattern to `/site/`.\n\n**Judgement calls against documented standards**\n\n- **`cli.py` publish/deploy versus `publish.site_build()`**: `cms publish` plus `cms deploy` never inserts a `site_builds` row. After a Site build from the command line, the dashboard keeps saying \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\". CONTEXT.md treats the Site build as one step, but there are now two routes to it and only one is recorded.\n- **Vocabulary (CONTEXT.md)**: In `guide.html`, \"This guide has no English version\" uses \"version\", which is an _Avoid_ word (the glossary's own term is English text). The test name `test_admin_puts_the_site_online_with_the_update_site_button` avoids saying Site build. Calling the push sub-step `deploy` is fine, since spec #1 uses \"Deploy (the git push)\" the same way.\n- **Tests (spec #1, Testing Decisions)**: these comply. They go through HTTP and `render_site(out)`, never DB rows.\n\n**Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n\n- **Mysterious Name / inconsistent naming:** `publish.site_build()`, the route `build_site`, the dependency `site_builder` and the capability `\"build_site\"`. That's four spellings of one concept.\n- **Duplicated Code:**\n  - `site_builder` repeats `web.admin_user` (`if not user.can(...): raise AdminRequired`). A shared `requires(capability)` would remove the copy.\n  - The other-language rule is written twice: `other = \"en\" if lang == \"zh\" else \"zh\"` in `publish.py`, and `{{ \"en\" if lang == \"zh\" else \"zh\" }}` in `base.html`.\n  - `{% if guides %}{{ guide_list(guides) }}{% else %}&lt;p&gt;{{ t.no_guides }}&lt;/p&gt;{% endif %}` appears in both `home.html` and `author.html`, so it could live inside the macro.\n  - Suppressed: `DeployFailed` copies the `Refused(message)` shape, but that is the repo's convention.\n- **Feature Envy:** `changes_not_on_site` loads every Published Guide through `guides.published(conn)` just to compare `updated_at`. A count query in `guides.py` would keep it next to the data.\n- **Divergent Change:** `publish.py` now changes for four unrelated reasons: rendering, the git subprocess, recording builds in the DB, and dashboard counts.\n- **Speculative Generality:**\n  - `_Writer(out, **shared: Any)` only ever receives `current_patch`.\n  - The default `deploy(..., message=\"Publish site\")` is never needed, because both callers pass their own value.\n- **Primitive Obsession:**\n  - `lang` is a bare `\"zh\"`/`\"en\"` string throughout.\n  - Page paths are strings whose meaning depends on a trailing `/` (`relative()`'s `target.endswith(\"/\") or not target`).\n\n**No issues found** on CSRF (the form has its token and the app-wide `verify_csrf` covers it), relative paths in published HTML, Markdown sanitizing (`attribute_filter` now also drops `/` and `\\` URLs), Published-only reads (`guides.published`), dependencies (only stdlib and the existing `ghp_import`), or secrets.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>62379</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>7</tool_uses><duration_ms>85238</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>\n</system-reminder>"}]}}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found one serious problem: the seven new page templates in `templates/site/` would not be committed. The root `.gitignore` line `site/` matches any folder named `site`, so it ignores `templates/site/` as well as the generated output. `git add -n templates/site` refuses and names `.gitignore:3`. The 21 T04/T00 tests (and all 138) pass here only because the files exist on this machine. On a fresh clone `render_site` fails, so every acceptance criterion breaks. The fix is to anchor the rule as `/site/`.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Failure reporting covers only the deploy.** Spec: \"runs the Site build plus the existing deploy, and reports success or failure.\" `app/routes/site.py` catches only `DeployFailed`. If `render_site` itself raises (a template error, a filesystem error), the Admin gets a 500 error instead of a message.\n- **The `cms deploy` CLI never resets the count.** Spec: \"shows 'N 项更改尚未更新到网站' until the next successful Site build.\" Only `site_build()` writes a `site_builds` row. In `CONTEXT.md`, a Site build is regenerating the site and putting it online, and #1 lists \"`cms publish` plus deploy, or the 更新网站 button\". So running `cms publish` then `cms deploy` leaves the dashboard count stale.\n\n**(b) Not asked for (scope creep)**\n- **New link filter in `app/rendering.py`.** `_no_root_absolute_urls` silently drops any `href`/`src` in user Markdown that starts with `/`, `//` or `\\`. It also changes the admin preview. It serves \"Every link is relative\", but it is a new content rule nobody asked for, and the writer is never warned (#1 has a preview-warnings mechanism for this kind of thing). It is borderline; it should at least be noted in the ticket.\n- **Small extras.** The CSS font and header changes, and the extra `en/` link on the root page, are cosmetic and harmless.\n\n**(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**\n- **The fallback notice is on the wrong page, in the wrong language.** Spec: \"If a Guide has no text in the other language, the switch links to its Hero's page there, with a notice.\" Story 94 says the switch should \"take me to … its Hero's page with a notice\". The code puts the notice in English, on the *Chinese* Guide page, before the Reader clicks. The English Hero page they land on has no notice at all.\n- **\"Newest Guides\" sorts by last edit, not publish date.** Spec: \"a home page with the Current Patch, the newest Guides\". `guides.published()` orders by `updated_at DESC`, so editing an old Published Guide moves it to the top. `published_at` is probably what \"newest\" means.\n- **The count only sees Guide changes.** #1 says the count \"compares content change times with the last successful Site build\". The code counts only Published Guides whose `updated_at` is newer. Hero name corrections and new Heroes or Patches change the site but never show up in the count. It is acceptable for #5's acceptance criterion (it goes up after a Publish), but the gap should be noted.\n\nEverything else checks out against #5:\n- the `zh/` and `en/` trees and the root redirect;\n- per-Guide pages at `guides/&lt;slug&gt;/`;\n- Hero pages grouped by Patch, newest first;\n- Author pages at `authors/&lt;id&gt;/` with the Display name only;\n- the English filter and the \"No English guides yet\" notices;\n- relative links;\n- sanitization;\n- the Admin-only button with CSRF;\n- the T00 tests still passing.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>62159</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>9</tool_uses><duration_ms>99516</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found one serious problem: the seven new page templates in `templates/site/` would not be committed. The root `.gitignore` line `site/` matches any folder named `site`, so it ignores `templates/site/` as well as the generated output. `git add -n templates/site` refuses and names `.gitignore:3`. The 21 T04/T00 tests (and all 138) pass here only because the files exist on this machine. On a fresh clone `render_site` fails, so every acceptance criterion breaks. The fix is to anchor the rule as `/site/`.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Failure reporting covers only the deploy.** Spec: \"runs the Site build plus the existing deploy, and reports success or failure.\" `app/routes/site.py` catches only `DeployFailed`. If `render_site` itself raises (a template error, a filesystem error), the Admin gets a 500 error instead of a message.\n- **The `cms deploy` CLI never resets the count.** Spec: \"shows 'N 项更改尚未更新到网站' until the next successful Site build.\" Only `site_build()` writes a `site_builds` row. In `CONTEXT.md`, a Site build is regenerating the site and putting it online, and #1 lists \"`cms publish` plus deploy, or the 更新网站 button\". So running `cms publish` then `cms deploy` leaves the dashboard count stale.\n\n**(b) Not asked for (scope creep)**\n- **New link filter in `app/rendering.py`.** `_no_root_absolute_urls` silently drops any `href`/`src` in user Markdown that starts with `/`, `//` or `\\`. It also changes the admin preview. It serves \"Every link is relative\", but it is a new content rule nobody asked for, and the writer is never warned (#1 has a preview-warnings mechanism for this kind of thing). It is borderline; it should at least be noted in the ticket.\n- **Small extras.** The CSS font and header changes, and the extra `en/` link on the root page, are cosmetic and harmless.\n\n**(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**\n- **The fallback notice is on the wrong page, in the wrong language.** Spec: \"If a Guide has no text in the other language, the switch links to its Hero's page there, with a notice.\" Story 94 says the switch should \"take me to … its Hero's page with a notice\". The code puts the notice in English, on the *Chinese* Guide page, before the Reader clicks. The English Hero page they land on has no notice at all.\n- **\"Newest Guides\" sorts by last edit, not publish date.** Spec: \"a home page with the Current Patch, the newest Guides\". `guides.published()` orders by `updated_at DESC`, so editing an old Published Guide moves it to the top. `published_at` is probably what \"newest\" means.\n- **The count only sees Guide changes.** #1 says the count \"compares content change times with the last successful Site build\". The code counts only Published Guides whose `updated_at` is newer. Hero name corrections and new Heroes or Patches change the site but never show up in the count. It is acceptable for #5's acceptance criterion (it goes up after a Publish), but the gap should be noted.\n\nEverything else checks out against #5:\n- the `zh/` and `en/` trees and the root redirect;\n- per-Guide pages at `guides/&lt;slug&gt;/`;\n- Hero pages grouped by Patch, newest first;\n- Author pages at `authors/&lt;id&gt;/` with the Display name only;\n- the English filter and the \"No English guides yet\" notices;\n- relative links;\n- sanitization;\n- the Admin-only button with CSRF;\n- the T00 tests still passing.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>62159</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>9</tool_uses><duration_ms>99516</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"},"uuid":"4b4bf1a2-1ae6-40d7-9c47-b5e8be4bb59f","timestamp":"2026-10-17T18:03:51.615Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"task-notification","producer":"session-task","runId":"0mvcpeol6-1c3ae6cb"},"promptSource":"system","turnOrigin":"task_notification","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":1,"turnIndex":3},"queueSkipAttachments":true,"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"15475bfa-45c3-4534-949f-2e433515bc06","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"425af19f-e331-4f23-af57-152599f31c4d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LAZXb98XTSPUpYJJdhKyVF","type":"tool_result","content":"50\t           \"no_guides\": \"No English guides yet.\", \"updated\": \"Updated\",\n51\t           \"other_language\": \"中文\"},\n52\t}\n53\tNEWEST_ON_HOME = 10\n54\t\n55\t\n56\tdef environment() -> Environment:\n57\t    env = Environment(\n58\t        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n59\t        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n60\t    )\n61\t    # `guide|localized(\"title\", lang)` is guide.title_zh or guide.title_en.\n62\t    env.filters[\"localized\"] = lambda item, field, lang: getattr(item, f\"{field}_{lang}\")\n63\t    env.filters[\"markdown\"] = render_markdown\n64\t    return env\n65\t\n66\t\n67\tdef by_patch(listed: list[guides.Guide]) -> list[tuple[str, list[guides.Guide]]]:\n68\t    \"\"\"Guides grouped by Patch, newest Patch first, keeping each group's order.\"\"\"\n69\t    ordered = sorted(listed, key=lambda guide: guide.patch_id, reverse=True)\n70\t    return [(patch_name, list(group)) for patch_name, group\n71\t            in itertools.groupby(ordered, key=lambda guide: guide.patch_name)]\n72\t\n73\t\n74\tdef relative(target: str, page: str) -> str:\n75\t    \"\"\"The relative link from the page at folder `page` to `target`. Both are\n76\t    paths from the site root; a folder ends in \"/\" (\"\" is the root itself).\"\"\"\n77\t    link = posixpath.relpath(target or \".\", page or \".\")\n78\t    return f\"{link}/\" if target.endswith(\"/\") or not target else link\n79\t\n80\t\n81\tclass _Writer:\n82\t    \"\"\"Writes pages into `out`. Each page can make relative links with\n83\t    `site_link(path from the root)` and, inside a language tree, with\n84\t    `link(path inside the tree)`. A page in a language tree also gets\n85\t    `switch_link`, the language switch: the same page in the other tree unless\n86\t    `switch_to` names another path inside that tree.\"\"\"\n87\t\n88\t    def __init__(self, out: Path, **shared: Any) -> None:\n89\t        self.out = out\n90\t        self.env = environment()\n91\t        self.shared = shared\n92\t\n93\t    def page(self, path: str, template: str, *, lang: str | None = None,\n94\t             switch_to: str | None = None, **context: Any) -> None:\n95\t        \"\"\"Write the page Readers get at `path`: \"\" for the root, or a folder\n96\t        such as \"zh/guides/vanessa-12/\".\"\"\"\n97\t        def site_link(target: str) -> str:\n98\t            return relative(target, path)\n99\t\n100\t        if lang:\n101\t            other = \"en\" if lang == \"zh\" else \"zh\"\n102\t            same_page = path.removeprefix(f\"{lang}/\")\n103\t            context |= {\"lang\": lang, \"t\": LABELS[lang],\n104\t                        \"link\": lambda target: site_link(f\"{lang}/{target}\"),\n105\t                        \"switch_link\": site_link(f\"{other}/{switch_to or same_page}\")}\n106\t        file = self.out / path / \"index.html\"\n107\t        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n108\t        file.write_text(self.env.get_template(template).render(\n109\t            site_link=site_link, **self.shared, **context))\n110\t\n111\t\n112\tdef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n113\t    out = out or settings.SITE\n114\t    if out.exists():\n115\t        shutil.rmtree(out)\n116\t    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n117\t    with db.connect() as conn:\n118\t        published = guides.published(conn)\n119\t        heroes = game.heroes(conn)\n120\t        patches = game.patches(conn)\n121\t    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n122\t    # `guide|localized(\"title\", lang)` is guide.title_zh or guide.title_en.\n    env.filters[\"localized\"] = lambda item, field, lang: getattr(item, f\"{field}_{lang}\")\n    env.filters[\"markdown\"] = render_markdown\n    return env\n\n\ndef by_patch(listed: list[guides.Guide]) -> list[tuple[str, list[guides.Guide]]]:\n    \"\"\"Guides grouped by Patch, newest Patch first, keeping each group's order.\"\"\"\n    ordered = sorted(listed, key=lambda guide: guide.patch_id, reverse=True)\n    return [(patch_name, list(group)) for patch_name, group\n            in itertools.groupby(ordered, key=lambda guide: guide.patch_name)]\n\n\ndef relative(target: str, page: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The relative link from the page at folder `page` to `target`. Both are\n    paths from the site root; a folder ends in \"/\" (\"\" is the root itself).\"\"\"\n    link = posixpath.relpath(target or \".\", page or \".\")\n    return f\"{link}/\" if target.endswith(\"/\") or not target else link\n\n\nclass _Writer:\n    \"\"\"Writes pages into `out`. Each page can make relative links with\n    `site_link(path from the root)` and, inside a language tree, with\n    `link(path inside the tree)`. A page in a language tree also gets\n    `switch_link`, the language switch: the same page in the other tree unless\n    `switch_to` names another path inside that tree.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, out: Path, **shared: Any) -> None:\n        self.out = out\n        self.env = environment()\n        self.shared = shared\n\n    def page(self, path: str, template: str, *, lang: str | None = None,\n             switch_to: str | None = None, **context: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Write the page Readers get at `path`: \"\" for the root, or a folder\n        such as \"zh/guides/vanessa-12/\".\"\"\"\n        def site_link(target: str) -> str:\n            return relative(target, path)\n\n        if lang:\n            other = \"en\" if lang == \"zh\" else \"zh\"\n            same_page = path.removeprefix(f\"{lang}/\")\n            context |= {\"lang\": lang, \"t\": LABELS[lang],\n                        \"link\": lambda target: site_link(f\"{lang}/{target}\"),\n                        \"switch_link\": site_link(f\"{other}/{switch_to or same_page}\")}\n        file = self.out / path / \"index.html\"\n        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        file.write_text(self.env.get_template(template).render(\n            site_link=site_link, **self.shared, **context))\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        published = guides.published(conn)\n        heroes = game.heroes(conn)\n        patches = game.patches(conn)\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    # Every Author with a Published Guide gets a page in both trees, even if\n    # none of their Guides has English text.\n    authors = {guide.author_id: guide.author_name for guide in published}\n    write = _Writer(out, current_patch=patches[0].name if patches else None)\n    write.page(\"\", \"site/root.html\")\n    for lang in LANGUAGES:\n        listed = [guide for guide in published if guide.has_text_in(lang)]\n        write.page(f\"{lang}/\", \"site/home.html\", lang=lang,\n                   guides=listed[:NEWEST_ON_HOME], heroes=heroes)\n        for hero in heroes:\n            write.page(f\"{lang}/heroes/{hero.slug}/\", \"site/hero.html\", lang=lang,\n                       hero=hero, patches=by_patch(\n                           [guide for guide in listed if guide.hero_id == hero.id]))\n        for author_id, author_name in authors.items():\n            write.page(f\"{lang}/authors/{author_id}/\", \"site/author.html\", lang=lang,\n                       author_name=author_name,\n                       guides=[guide for guide in listed if guide.author_id == author_id])\n        for guide in listed:\n            # Only English can be missing, since Chinese text is required.\n            missing = not guide.has_text_in(\"en\")\n            write.page(f\"{lang}/guides/{guide.slug}/\", \"site/guide.html\",\n                       lang=lang, guide=guide, no_english=missing,\n                       switch_to=f\"heroes/{guide.hero_slug}/\" if missing else None)\n    return out\n\n\nclass DeployFailed(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The push to gh-pages failed; the message says why.\"\"\"","numLines":100,"startLine":50,"totalLines":184}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"15475bfa-45c3-4534-949f-2e433515bc06","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

only the generated output is ignored now |\n| \"This guide has no English **version**\": *version* is an Avoid word | **Fixed.** Reworded to \"has no English text yet\" |\n| Four spellings of one concept (`site_build`, `build_site`, `site_builder`, capability `build_site`) | **Fixed.** `publish.build_site()`, capability `build_site`, dependency `site_builder`, and the route handler is now `update_site` (the 更新网站 button) |\n| Duplicated other-language rule in `publish.py` and `base.html` | **Fixed.** Computed once and passed to templates as `other` |\n| Duplicated \"list or empty notice\" branch in the home and Author templates | **Fixed.** Moved into the `guide_list` macro |\n| Speculative `_Writer(out, **shared)` | **Fixed.** Now an explicit `current_patch` parameter |\n| `site_builder` repeats the shape of `web.admin_user` | **Left as is.** It checks a different capability; a generic `requires(capability)` can come when a third one is needed |\n| Possible Feature Envy: `changes_not_on_site` loads Published Guides to compare times | **Left as is.** It keeps Guide SQL inside `app/guides.py`, and the site is small |\n| Possible Divergent Change in `publish.py`; `lang` as a bare string; unused default deploy message | **Left as is.** Spec #1 places the deploy and the build record with `render_site`. `build_site()` does use the default message |\n\n### Spec\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Fallback notice was on the Chinese Guide page instead of the English Hero page the Reader lands on | **Fixed.** The switch links to `en/heroes/<slug>/#no-english-text`, and the English Hero page has a notice with that id that shows only when the Reader arrives through that link (CSS `:target`, no JS). Test updated |\n| \"Newest Guides\" sorted by last edit, so an Admin's typo fix moved an old Guide to the top | **Fixed** (test first). The home page now sorts by publish time |\n| `cms publish` + `cms deploy` from the CLI doesn't reset the \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\" count | **Known gap.** #1 says \"the CLI commands stay as they are\"; only the 更新网站 button records a Site build |\n| Only a failed deploy is reported; an error while rendering gives a 500 | **Left as is.** A failed push is the expected failure (story 88). A render error is a bug and should show up loudly |\n| Scope: `render_markdown` now drops `href`/`src` values starting with `/`, `//` or `\\` | **Kept.** Without it, a writer's `[x](/foo)` would break the criterion \"No generated file contains `href=\\\"/`\". It applies to the preview too, so the preview still matches the site. A preview warning for this could be added later |\n| The count covers only Published Guides, not Hero or Patch changes | **Known gap.** It meets this ticket's criterion; later tickets (Unpublish, Trash, Pages) extend what counts |\n\nTests: 18 new tests in `tests/test_t04_site_build.py`, covering Seam 2 (`render_site` output) and Seam 1 (the button with the deploy step replaced). Full suite: 139 passed. pyright: 0 errors.\nEOF\n)\"","description":"Post review findings and resolutions on issue #5"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":981,"cache_read_input_tokens":188387,"output_tokens":1546,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":95},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":981,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1546,"cache_read_input_tokens":188387,"cache_creation_input_tokens":981,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":981},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01DmciszdNM62TZiWeXd8Fju":{"command":"gh issue comment 5 --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## /code-review findings (T04) and how each was resolved\n\nTwo parallel reviews: **Standards** (CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST, ADRs, plus a code-smell baseline) and **Spec** (this issue, with #1 for context).\n\n### Standards\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| **Hard:** `.gitignore` line `site/` also ignored `templates/site/`, so the new public-site templates would never be committed and a clean clone's Site build would fail | **Fixed.** Anchored to `/site/`; {"parentUuid":"f64d73b2-136b-40fa-bdda-37f27e5db2ea","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg8FfHwXnvf23osREk2kb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T04 (#5) is built and committed as `253834e` on the current branch. Nothing is pushed. All 139 tests pass and pyright reports no errors.\n\n**What now happens**\n- **The site:** `render_site` writes a Chinese tree (`zh/`) and an English tree (`en/`) from Published Guides only, and the root `index.html` sends Readers to `zh/`. Each language has:\n  - a home page with the Current Patch, the newest Guides and a grid of Heroes;\n  - a page per Guide at `guides/<slug>/`;\n  - a page per Hero, with its Guides grouped by Patch, newest Patch first;\n  - a page per Author at `authors/<id>/`, showing the Display name and never the email.\n- **English tree:** a Chinese-only Guide is left out of `en/`. Hero and Author pages still exist there, showing \"No English guides yet\" when empty.\n- **Language switch:** it sits top right and links to the same page in the other language. On a Chinese-only Guide it goes to that Hero's English page instead, and a notice appears there only when the Reader arrives through that link.\n- **Links:** every link is relative. A writer's own `/foo` link or image in Markdown is now dropped when the Markdown is cleaned, both in the preview and on the site, so it can't break the \"no `href=\"/`\" rule.\n- **更新网站 button:** Admin only. It rebuilds the site, pushes it, and shows success or git's error message. The dashboard shows \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\", or \"网站已是最新\" when nothing is waiting.\n\n**Changes you should know about**\n- **`.gitignore`:** the review found that its `site/` line also matched `templates/site/`, so the new page templates would have been silently left out of the commit. I changed it to `/site/`.\n- **Timestamps:** Guide timestamps now record milliseconds. Without that, a Guide published in the same second as a site update wouldn't be counted as a change waiting to go online.\n- **Tests can't push:** `tests/conftest.py` now replaces the push step and points the site folder at a temp directory for every test.\n\n**Review**\nI posted the findings and how each was handled as a comment on #5. Most are fixed. Two gaps I left on purpose:\n- Running `cms publish` then `cms deploy` from the command line doesn't reset the dashboard count; only the button does. The spec says the CLI commands stay as they are.\n- The count only covers Published Guides, not changes to Heroes or Patches.\n\n**Other session's work**\nAnother session committed to this branch while I worked (Exercise A and B). Its `notes/usage-ledger.csv` changes and transcripts 07–08 are still uncommitted, and I left them out of my commit.\n\nI checked the site by rendering the demo data and reading the output. I didn't open it in a browser."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1051,"cache_read_input_tokens":190984,"output_tokens":953,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":20},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1051,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":953,"cache_read_input_tokens":190984,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1051,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1051},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg8FfHaxDjEpPa2tmUuZV","requestRef":"0054b5f3-a947-43df-9d17-1c130399db40","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"758e28a1-6c8a-4223-a2d0-06456a03f82c","timestamp":"2026-10-17T18:06:26.946Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"8e04d881-36e8-4648-80fb-a97808a23dee","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

Correcting its Official names no longer moves its page or the Guide Slugs built from it. Because the Slug no longer catches a clashing edit, there is a new rule: no two Heroes share an English Official name, ignoring case.\n\n```diff\n add_hero(name_zh, name_en)\n   check both names are filled in\n+  refuse if another Hero has this English name (casefold)\n   slug = slugify(name_en)\n   refuse if another Hero has this slug\n   insert\n\n edit_hero(hero_id, name_zh, name_en)\n   check both names are filled in\n-  slug = slugify(name_en)\n-  refuse if another Hero has this slug\n-  update names and slug\n+  refuse if another Hero has this English name (casefold)\n+  update names only","is_error":false}]}}
